subject: english-literature
title: Setting the Scene
welcome_lead: The area Time & Space asks how historical and cultural context shapes meaning. Setting is never mere backdrop — it produces character and theme.
meta_desc: English Literature: historical context, setting, and psychogeography in literary analysis.
final_note: Where and when a text was written shapes what it can mean.

concepts.def: The time, place and social environment in which a text is set.
The study of how geographical environments shape emotional and psychological states.
The political, social and cultural moment of a work's composition.
Bakhtin's term for the time-space configuration of a genre.
Detailed depiction of regional customs, dialect and landscape.
The distinct character and emotional resonance attached to a particular location.

walkthroughs.body_html: Each genre has a typical time-space configuration: the road in picaresque, the castle in gothic, the salon in society fiction. Identifying the chronotope clarifies generic expectations.
Walking London with Mrs Dalloway shows how streets evoke memory. Dickens uses fog in Bleak House as both atmosphere and metaphor for legal obscurity.
Reading Things Fall Apart without knowing British colonialism in Nigeria misses Achebe's intervention. Context isn't optional decoration — it grounds interpretation.
